title: Floating and sinking
examples: Why do some things float even if they are heavy?
What makes a boat stay on top of the water?
If I put a rock and a leaf in water, which one will sink?

explain.say: Today we are learning about things that float and things that sink.

items: Sinking things go to the bottom.

explain.say: Some things are heavy for their size, like a big rock.
Boats are shaped in a special way that helps them float.
We can test objects by carefully putting them in water.

items: Observe if it floats or sinks

explain.say: A big, hollow log floats because it pushes water out of the way.
When you play in a bathtub, you are testing if toys float or sink.

faq.q: Why does a big boat float if it is made of heavy metal?
faq.a: The shape of the boat pushes enough water out that the water pushes back up, keeping it afloat. It is not just about the material.
asks: What keeps a ship from sinking?

faq.q: Is it true that all heavy things sink?
faq.a: No, the shape matters a lot. Some things can be heavy but still float if they are shaped correctly.

faq.q: What is the difference between floating and sinking?
faq.a: Floating means the object stays on top of the water surface. Sinking means the object goes down to the bottom.
asks: What does it mean to float?

faq.q: Does the size of an object decide if it floats?
faq.a: Size is part of it, but the shape and how much water it pushes are more important for floating.
asks: Is size the only thing that matters?

faq.q: If I use a piece of wood and a stone, which one will float?
faq.a: The piece of wood will float because its shape and material are less dense than water. The stone will sink.

facts: Sinking objects are heavier than the water they push.
Boat shapes trap air, which helps them float.
Density helps explain why things float or sink.

quiz.say: A large, hollow pumpkin is placed in a pool. What will happen?

options.show: The pumpkin will float only if it is small.
options.say: The pumpkin will float only if it is small.

options.show: The pumpkin will float because it is light.
options.say: The pumpkin will float because it is light.

quiz.why: The pumpkin's hollow shape pushes enough water out of the way to keep it afloat.

wrong.0: This is wrong because size is not the only thing that matters for floating.
wrong.1: This is wrong because even if it is light, the shape is what helps it float.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the air trapped inside makes it float.

quiz.say: A small metal key is dropped into a bucket of water. What happens?

options.show: The key will float because it is small.
options.say: The key will float because it is small.

options.show: The key will float because it is metal.
options.say: The key will float because it is metal.

options.show: The key will float if I blow on it.
options.say: The key will float if I blow on it.

quiz.why: Metal is usually denser than water, so the key sinks to the bottom.

wrong.1: This is wrong because size does not decide if something sinks.
wrong.2: This is wrong because being made of metal usually makes it sink.
wrong.3: This is wrong because blowing only moves it, it does not change its density.

quiz.say: A large, solid wooden block is placed in water. What happens?

options.show: The wood block will sink because it is large.
options.say: The wood block will sink because it is large.

options.show: The wood block will sink because it is solid.
options.say: The wood block will sink because it is solid.

options.show: The wood block will float only if it is cut into pieces.
options.say: The wood block will float only if it is cut into pieces.

quiz.why: Wood is less dense than water, so the block floats on the surface.

wrong.1: This is wrong because being large does not mean it sinks.
wrong.2: This is wrong because solid things can still float if they are light enough.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the whole block can float if it is made of wood.
